paragraphs: Friend, here's the lesson I want you to take out of this one. Two kinds of water showed up in this passage, and the people picked the wrong one. The LORD says they rejected "the gently flowing waters of Shiloah" and rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah instead (Isaiah 8:6). When you trade the God who is gentle and steady for a threat that looks big, you end up with a flood, and that's a rough swap.

Now look at what the LORD does with it. He had Isaiah write a name on a large scroll, and He said He would appoint trustworthy witnesses for Himself, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah (Isaiah 8:1-2). The name came with a clock: before the boy knows how to cry "Father" or "Mother," the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off by the king of Assyria (Isaiah 8:4). The LORD says it first and has it written down, so nobody is left guessing.

So here's what this means for you, baker. People will huddle, prepare for battle, and prepare for battle AGAIN, and the message says they will be shattered (Isaiah 8:9). Their plans get thwarted and their proposals do not happen, because "God is with us" (Isaiah 8:10). When the noise around you gets loud and the plans of the world look big, that last line is the one to hold onto. I've been in the dark long enough to know that you want the One who is with you, and I'm glad He is.
